body:
Myk asked for "an up-to-date document of this system's capabilities — the long tedious read, organized by chapter, probably with visuals (draw from the deck you built the other day for how we visualize deltas)." The deck he means is `demos/tutorial/intro.html`, shipped at <https://bombadil-labs.github.io/loam/intro.html> and linked from the tutorial landing.

**The load-bearing word is UP-TO-DATE, and it is the whole ticket.** A hand-maintained capabilities document reproduces T81's failure (the README documented the opposite of the code) at twenty-eight sections' scale, and it reproduces it silently — nobody discovers a stale chapter until a stranger reads it and is wrong. So the deliverable is not prose; it is prose WIRED TO A RAIL, on the two precedents already in the tree:

- `test/site/arc.test.ts` — "The page and this test share one arc — that identity IS the anti-rot guarantee." The test imports the exact module the page renders from.
- `test/docs/node-floor.test.ts` and T81's executable README fence — a documented fact asserted against the code that makes it true.

**SHAPE.** The chapters are DATA, in `demos/capabilities/chapters.mjs`, imported by both the page and the rail. Each chapter carries sections; each section carries `claims`, and every claim is a triple:

- `says` — the sentence the book asserts, in a reader's language;
- `spec` — the `spec/NN-slug.md` section that decided it, with its § number;
- `proof` — a test path, or a named export from `src/index.ts`, that makes it true.

That is spec-lint's rule turned outward: *every promise names the test that proves it.* A claim with no proof is a WISH, and the rail fails it — the same verdict spec-lint gives a criterion with no verification method.

**THE ANTI-ROT ENGINE is the COVERAGE assertion, not the citation checks.** Checking that a cited path exists only catches a claim that rotted; the rail that keeps the book current is the other direction: *every file in `spec/` must be cited by at least one claim.* A landing that adds `spec/32-*.md` turns the suite red until the book gains a paragraph about it — so the document cannot fall behind the spec without failing CI, which is the only mechanism that has ever kept a doc honest here. Pair it with the door check (every export a claim names is really exported from `src/index.ts`, imported for real, not grepped) and staleness has two ways to go red and none to go quiet.

**VISUALS.** Lift the deck's drawing kit into `demos/capabilities/figures.mjs`: the node/edge/PORT renderer, and the palette — ground `#141009`, alice amber, bob blue, entity green, prim parchment, dead vermilion, serif prose over mono labels. The port convention is the part worth preserving verbatim: an edge grips a node at a small solid dot, a port on a delta is one of its pointers and a port on an object is one of its properties, and edges from different deltas that bind the SAME property converge on ONE dot — the conflict is drawn rather than described. Do NOT refactor `intro.html` to import the module: it is copied to `site-dist/` unbundled and self-contained on purpose, and reaching into it would trade a working page for a tidy one. Two copies of a drawing kit is the right price for a page that survives with no build.

**REGISTER.** A book, not a deck and not the spec. `SPEC.md` is organized by landing order for a builder and says what IS in the vocabulary of the implementation; this is organized pedagogically for someone deciding whether Loam is for them, and every term it introduces is defined where it first appears. Myk has said twice that the dense-JSON register loses him — the test of a chapter is whether it reads aloud.

**CHAPTERS** (draft; the coverage rail decides the final partition, since every spec file must land in one): the ground and the delta — objects nobody creates — reading, and why resolution is the application's business — disagreement, negation, and the two levels a reader can be lied to at — the gateway as the only surface — capabilities, accounts, tenants — containers, trust, and posture — erasure and what a proof of forgetting costs — federation and what crosses a boundary — apps as deltas: schemas, resolvers, renderers, the MCP door — running one: migration, health, the CLI, the browser peer.

**HOME.** `demos/capabilities/`, built by `scripts/build-site.mjs` into `site-dist/capabilities.html` and linked from the tutorial landing beside the intro deck. NOT root markdown — CLAUDE.md holds root to four docs, and this is the fifth thing that would have wanted in.

**FOLD IN A GAP FOUND WHILE SCOPING THIS:** `build.test.ts` asserts the site artifact holds together and does not list `intro.html`, though the landing links it — delete the `cpSync` in `build-site.mjs` and the link 404s with a green bar. Add both the deck and the book to that suite's artifact list.

**CARE.** The container chapter's vocabulary is mid-rename (`posture: "wall" | "property"` → `"separate" | "shared"`, Myk's call, in flight). Write the new names and land after the rename, or cite the section rather than the field.

**DESIGN QUESTIONS FOR MYK:** (a) does a chapter get to say what Loam CANNOT do yet — an honest "not built" register, which would make the book usable as an evaluation document and would also mean the book cites tickets, not only spec; (b) one page or one page per chapter (one page is a truer "long tedious read" and is trivially searchable in a browser).
title: The capabilities book — a chaptered read of what Loam can do, that goes red when it goes stale
